title: U.S. Open — Shinnecock Hills
subtitle: A day inside the 126th U.S. Open
recap: A summer day at Shinnecock Hills during the 2026 U.S. Open, taking in the championship grounds, clubhouse views and the atmosphere around one of golf’s most historic venues.
personalNote: The day became part of the collection when Auburn golfer Jackson Koivun signed the U.S. Open hat — connecting a memorable championship visit directly to a piece of memorabilia from the experience.

title: Mets vs. Yankees
subtitle: Subway Series
recap: The Mets jumped on the Yankees with Brandon Nimmo’s first-inning grand slam and never stopped adding on in a 12–6 Subway Series win. Pete Alonso homered twice and drove in five, while Francisco Lindor added an RBI single and scored twice. New York broke the game open with four more runs in the seventh as the Mets turned a crosstown rivalry game into one of the biggest offensive performances in the archive.
personalNote: A Subway Series day at Citi Field — arriving at the ballpark, walking the concourse, watching warmups and sharing a Mets–Yankees game together.

title: Auburn vs. Kentucky
subtitle: A Historic Win at Rupp
recap: No. 1 Auburn delivered a landmark road win at Rupp Arena, taking control with a 49–34 first half and beating No. 17 Kentucky 94–78. Miles Kelly erupted for 30 points and tied an Auburn record with nine three-pointers, while Chad Baker-Mazara scored 22 and Tahaad Pettiford added 21. Auburn led by as many as 22, won at Rupp for the first time since 1988 and clinched at least a share of the SEC regular-season championship.
personalNote: A family road trip to Rupp Arena for No. 1 Auburn against Kentucky — from arriving in Lexington and seeing the arena, to the pregame atmosphere, family photos in Auburn gear, the final scoreboard and a memorable interaction near the floor. Auburn’s first win at Rupp since 1988 made the trip even more special.

title: Auburn vs. Duke
subtitle: ACC/SEC Challenge
recap: Two top teams traded runs in one of the season’s marquee early matchups at Cameron Indoor Stadium. Duke took a 43–36 halftime lead and Auburn kept pressing in the second half, but the Blue Devils answered enough of the Tigers’ pushes to finish an 84–78 win. Cooper Flagg led Duke with 22 points and 11 rebounds; Johni Broome answered with 20 points and 12 rebounds for Auburn, and Tahaad Pettiford scored 20 off the bench.
personalNote: A road trip to Cameron Indoor Stadium for Auburn–Duke — from the retired-jersey displays and pregame views to the family photos in one of college basketball’s most famous arenas.
leaders: Auburn: Tahaad Pettiford — 20 points off the bench

title: Knicks vs. Pacers
subtitle: Knicks Home Opener
recap: Madison Square Garden’s home opener turned into a statement win. The Knicks took a one-point lead after the first quarter, then overwhelmed Indiana 36–21 in the second and 34–19 in the third to build a 31-point advantage. Jalen Brunson scored 26, Karl-Anthony Towns had 21 points and 15 rebounds in his MSG home debut, and New York held the Pacers to just 3-for-30 from three in a 123–98 victory.
personalNote: A New York night with the boys built around the Knicks home opener — walking toward Madison Square Garden, grabbing dinner, checking out Knicks memorabilia, settling into the seats and watching New York pull away from Indiana. The photos preserve the whole experience around the game, not just the final score.
leaders: Knicks: Jalen Brunson — 26 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists

title: Braves vs. Blue Jays
subtitle: Atlanta Baseball
recap: Atlanta did all of its scoring in the second inning and made the early burst stand up in a 3–1 win over Toronto. Max Fried delivered seven strong innings, allowing just one unearned run while striking out eight. The bullpen protected the two-run lead from there, and Raisel Iglesias closed the ninth for the save.

title: Ole Miss vs. Georgia Tech
subtitle: Oxford, The Grove & a Rebel Win
recap: Ole Miss led 24–10 after three quarters, but Georgia Tech made it a one-score game early in the fourth. That challenge triggered an explosive finish: the Rebels poured in 24 fourth-quarter points and pulled away for a 48–23 win in Oxford. Jaxson Dart hurt Georgia Tech with both his arm and his legs, and his 68-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Watkins helped break the game open late.
personalNote: A full Ole Miss game-day weekend preserved from Oxford — walking through the Walk of Champions, taking in The Grove and the Square, spending time together at the tailgate, and then heading into Vaught-Hemingway for the game. The photographs capture the entire experience around the 48–23 win over Georgia Tech, from the family moments before kickoff to the stadium at night.

Ole Miss: Jordan Watkins — 119 receiving yards

title: Auburn vs. Mercer
subtitle: Auburn Trip
recap: Auburn opened the 2022 season by scoring touchdowns on each of its first six scoring drives and beating Mercer 42–16. The Tigers led 28–7 at halftime and added two more touchdowns in the third quarter before weather interrupted the night. Jarquez Hunter ran for three touchdowns, Tank Bigsby added two more, and Auburn finished with 497 yards of offense.

title: Auburn vs. Ole Miss
subtitle: Auburn Weekend
recap: Auburn beat Ole Miss 20–14 in a tense SEC night at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Bo Nix threw for a career-high 340 yards and Auburn built a 20–7 lead through three quarters, but Ole Miss scored in the fourth and got the ball back with a chance to win. Christian Tutt’s interception on the final play sealed the victory and ended the comeback threat.
personalNote: An Auburn weekend that was about much more than the final score — campus, Toomer’s Corner, the stadium, Auburn traditions and time together around the Ole Miss game.

title: NL Wild Card Game
subtitle: Mets vs. Giants
recap: The 2016 National League Wild Card Game was a classic pitchers’ duel between Noah Syndergaard and Madison Bumgarner. Syndergaard struck out 10 over seven scoreless innings and Bumgarner matched him all night. The game remained 0–0 into the ninth before Conor Gillaspie hit a three-run homer, and Bumgarner finished a four-hit complete-game shutout to send San Francisco on with a 3–0 win.
personalNote: A postseason night at Citi Field with the kids — the atmosphere, the seats near the field and a winner-take-all Mets playoff game preserved as part of the family sports archive.

The result gave the Royals a 3–1 series lead and made this one of the most dramatic postseason nights preserved in the archive.

title: Rangers vs. Islanders
subtitle: Family Night at Nassau Coliseum
recap: A memorable Rangers–Islanders rivalry game at Nassau Coliseum turned into a wild third-period comeback. The Islanders led 5–3 early in the third, but Derek Stepan and Martin St. Louis scored 97 seconds apart to tie it. Kevin Klein completed the comeback with the game-winner at 15:28, giving the Rangers a 6–5 victory in a game that featured five third-period goals.

title: 2015 Outback Bowl
subtitle: Auburn vs. Wisconsin
recap: Auburn and Wisconsin traded momentum all afternoon in a New Year’s Day thriller that needed overtime. Auburn went ahead 31–28 on Cameron Artis-Payne’s touchdown with 2:55 left, but Rafael Gaglianone tied it with a 29-yard field goal with seven seconds remaining. Wisconsin then opened overtime with Gaglianone’s 25-yard field goal and held Auburn on its possession for a 34–31 win. Melvin Gordon powered the Badgers with 251 rushing yards and three touchdowns.
